extraction.name: Microsoft COCO: Common Objects in Context
extraction.description: A large-scale dataset for object recognition and scene understanding, containing complex everyday scenes with common objects in their natural context. Objects are labeled using per-instance segmentations for precise object localization. The dataset includes 91 common object categories with 2.5 million labeled instances in 328,000 images, collected via extensive crowd worker involvement.
extraction.creator: Tsung-Yi Lin, Michael Maire, Serge Belongie, Lubomir Bourdev, Ross Girshick, James Hays, Pietro Perona, Deva Ramanan, C. Lawrence Zitnick, Piotr Dollár
extraction.citeAs: Lin, T.-Y., Maire, M., Belongie, S., Bourdev, L., Girshick, R., Hays, J., Perona, P., Ramanan, D., Zitnick, C. L., & Dollár, P. (2014). Microsoft COCO: Common Objects in Context. arXiv:1405.0312.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Images were collected using a combination of Flickr searches for non-iconic images and pairwise object/scene category queries. Crowd workers on Amazon Mechanical Turk were used for category detection, instance spotting, and instance segmentation. The dataset emphasizes non-iconic views of objects in natural contexts with rich contextual relationships.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Crowdsourcing, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images were sourced from Flickr and web-based image searches, with filtering to remove iconic images and near-duplicates. Non-iconic images were prioritized by querying for pairs of object categories or object-scene pairs.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were filtered to remove near-duplicates and grouped by photographer and date taken to minimize duplicates across splits. Non-iconic images were prioritized, and iconic images were explicitly filtered out when necessary.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three-stage annotation pipeline: (1) Category labeling using hierarchical approach with 8 workers per image, (2) Instance spotting with 8 workers per image, and (3) Instance segmentation with training tasks for workers. Segmentations were verified by multiple workers, and poor-quality segmentations were discarded.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Worker quality was analyzed by comparing precision and recall of AMT workers against expert workers. The union of 8 AMT workers achieved higher recall than any expert, and worker precision was high for those completing the most jobs. Borderline segmentations were verified with multiple workers, and those failing quality checks were discarded.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 8 (for category labeling and instance spotting), 1 (for instance segmentation)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Dataset was split into two releases (2014 and 2015) with versioning information. The 2014 release included 82,783 training, 40,504 validation, and 40,775 testing images. The cumulative 2015 release included 165,482 training, 81,208 validation, and 81,434 testing images. Annotations for train and validation data were released, but not for test. The dataset is maintained and updated via the project website (mscoco.org).
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Person instances are included in the dataset, which may contain sensitive attributes such as gender, age, and appearance.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to advance object recognition and scene understanding, which can have broad applications in computer vision. However, the inclusion of person instances raises privacy considerations.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may contain biases due to the selection of object categories, the emphasis on non-iconic images, and the reliance on crowd workers for annotations. The dataset includes fewer iconic images, which may introduce biases toward non-canonical views of objects.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to 91 common object categories and does not include 'stuff' categories (e.g., sky, grass). Some categories were omitted in the 2014 release due to ambiguity or difficulty in labeling (e.g., hat, shoe, mirror). The dataset may not generalize well to fine-grained or rare object categories.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, and Fine-Tuning for object detection, instance segmentation, and scene understanding tasks. The dataset is designed to push research in contextual reasoning and precise object localization.
